turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on through, we'll sort your observations before the doctor. Your partner's waiting outside, is that right?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I told him to stay out there. I barely slept, and the traffic was a nightmare, so I'm not in the mood for a crowd.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Understood. Arm relaxed. Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy-four, pulse eighty-six, temperature thirty-six point seven, oxygen saturations ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I still feel awful, if those are meant to be comforting.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): They're reassuring from my side. Reception said you'd had a positive pregnancy test?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Two of them, at home, both positive. And I've been spotting. That's why I'm here.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Shah. Sorry you've waited. I've got the positive tests and the spotting. Tell me how it's been, in your own words.

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm pregnant, going by the tests, and there's blood. Pink, sometimes brown. Not floods, a liner's enough. It's been about a week... no, more like ten days. I think. The days are blurring, I'm that tired.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Staining for about ten days, not flooding. Any clots?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No clots. I keep nipping to the loo to check. It's doing my head in.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about pain? Any cramps, or pain off to one side?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not really. It's the blood I'm worried about, not pain.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sickness, sore breasts, things like that?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Breasts are sore, yeah. Sickness, no. I'm not being sick.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): When was your last period? A rough window is fine.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I can't give you a date. It was around Diwali, or after. Might've been the week after. We weren't writing it down.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Around Diwali or a bit later, and no exact day. I won't invent how many weeks that is. Any long-term problems, diabetes, epilepsy, anything of that sort?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I'm usually well. This is the problem.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): And medicines? Vitamins, or anything from the chemist, count as well.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid. I started the four hundred microgram tablets, but no, they switched me, it's five milligrams once a day. My sister's baby had spina bifida, so the midwife put me on the higher dose.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stay on the five milligrams, that's the right dose for you. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I'm aware of.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): How are you holding up with it all?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Worried sick. I was up half the night googling miscarriage, I'm shattered, and I'm snappy. Sorry.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please don't apologise for being frightened. May I feel your tummy?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, alright.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Soft. Tender low down in the middle, no tenderness out to either side, and no guarding. I'll bring your partner in for the plan, if that's okay.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. He'll only get worse out there on his own.

[SEG0029] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, I wasn't listening in, the telly was on some auction thing. She's been playing it down, doctor. She's dizzy every time she stands up, and the bleeding's heavier than a bit of spotting.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't. It is not heavier, it's spotting, I've already said. And I am not dizzy. I got up too fast and I was tired, the room did not spin. Stop talking for me.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm writing down what each of you describes, separately. Can I come back to the pain? You said there wasn't any.

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I know, and that was me being short. I've had cramps since yesterday, low down, like a period, nagging. It's in the middle, not off to one side. Walking sets it off. Lying down eases it. I'm not doubled over.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that's much clearer. Did you take anything for them?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol this morning. I was going to say a gram, but no, it was five hundred milligrams, one tablet. It barely touched it.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): One five hundred milligram tablet. And the sickness, you said you weren't being sick. Still the case?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Well, actually, I have been. I threw up before we left, and most mornings this week. I just couldn't be bothered to list it all. Can we get on.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Most mornings, this past week. Any pain at the tip of your shoulder, any fainting, any burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No shoulder pain. I haven't fainted. Weeing's fine, no burning.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink alcohol?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. I stopped the drinking when the test was positive.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Before that it was about two glasses of wine at the weekend, not on weeknights. I'm not trying to get her in trouble.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends, yeah. That part's fair. Don't gloat.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll be straight with you. My working impression is a threatened miscarriage, with spotting and cramps this early, and that is provisional, not a conclusion. I also can't rule out an ectopic until we've scanned, even though the pain is central, which is somewhat against it.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Ectopic. Fantastic. Just what I needed today.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Saying it out loud isn't me deciding that's what it is. This afternoon there'll be a pelvic ultrasound in the early pregnancy unit, and bloods today: the pregnancy hormone, a full blood count, and your blood group.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the bloods in here before you go down. Did you manage breakfast?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Toast, hours ago. Just do them. I'd rather the scan than more talking.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you soak a pad in an hour, if the pain becomes severe or one-sided, if you feel faint, or if shoulder pain starts, go straight to A&E and don't wait. Otherwise I'll see you back here in two days with the results.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days. And if I start panicking in the night?
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ring the early pregnancy unit, the number is on this leaflet, or come straight in. You don't have to sit it out until the two days if you're frightened or things change.
[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll stay with her tonight. We'll be back in two days unless it kicks off.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Arm's there. I'm done.
[SEG0053] person_1 (NURSE): Sharp scratch. Little tubes, then you're free to go downstairs for the scan.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): When the pictures are back we'll sit down and go through them. And if you can, leave the googling alone tonight.

spec.situation: Woman about 8-10 weeks pregnant with spotting and cramps; unsure of dates ('the last period was around Diwali, or after'); anxious; partner waits outside then joins. Scan and blood tests planned today, strict return advice.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

bad.reason: Dose and indication supported; 'currently_used' wrong since it was one-off this morning.

omissions.text: Home pregnancy testing was two tests at home, both positive.
Vaginal bleeding was described as pink or sometimes brown, and not heavy enough to flood pads; a liner is enough.
The patient initially denied pain but later clarified she has had low central period-like nagging cramps since yesterday, is not doubled over, and pain is central rather than one-sided.
Nausea/sickness was initially denied and then corrected: she had vomited before leaving home and on most mornings this week.
Negative finding: no current pain initially reported ('No. Not really.'), later revised by the patient.
Negative finding: no smoking and alcohol stopped when the pregnancy test was positive was reported by the patient; the weekend alcohol intake before that was only confirmed by the family member.
Examination detail omitted: there was no tenderness out to either side (bilateral/lateral abdominal tenderness absent), specifically described with low central tenderness.
The doctor said the pelvic ultrasound would be this afternoon in the early pregnancy unit.
The nurse stated bloods would be taken in the room before the patient went down for the scan, and later that she was free to go downstairs for the scan after the blood draw.
Safety-netting/follow-up detail: if panicking in the night, the patient was told to ring the early pregnancy unit using the leaflet number or come straight in rather than wait for the two-day review.
Plan detail: when the scan pictures are back, the doctor will sit down and go through them.
Recorded wrongly: 'dizziness on standing' is listed as a present symptom, but the patient explicitly denied dizziness; this was only reported by the family member and disputed by the patient.
